name: StandardAero, Inc.
reason: Engine aftermarket MRO with OEM-licensed positions and a growing installed base, but only a short post-IPO record of GAAP profit (EPS $0.04 to $0.83), EBIT margin at a 100th-percentile 9.6%, 10y avg ROIC 1.7%, acquisitions at 2.1x FCF and 2.8x net debt/EBITDA make the long-run economics hard to pin down.

name: Amentum Holdings, Inc.
reason: Merger-built government services contractor with a 3.5% EBIT margin, negative 10y ROIC/ROE, acquisitions at 3.5x FCF and 3.65x net debt/EBITDA; GAAP EPS only $0.27 vs huge adjusted add-backs and dependence on federal budget/contract recompetes - ordinary and levered.

name: Ingram Micro Holding Corporation
reason: Thin-margin IT distributor (EBIT margin 1.8%, 10y max 2.0%) with GAAP EPS down 12.6%/yr over 5y and at 0.14x its 2022 peak; low FCF conversion (0.37) and no moat beyond scale - a cheap but not special business.

name: Venture Global, Inc.
reason: LNG exporter whose earnings depend on spot LNG/gas spreads and large-scale project execution (EBIT margin fell from 61% to 37%), with 5.5x net debt/EBITDA, deeply negative FCF conversion (-2.9) and ongoing customer contract-arbitration litigation.

name: Smithfield Foods, Inc.
reason: Pork processor driven by the hog/commodity protein cycle (EPS fell to $0.04 in 2023) now at 1.0x its 10y EPS peak with EBIT margin at a history-high 8.8%; revenue CAGR ~1% and consensus EPS growth negative.

name: Sandisk Corporation
reason: NAND flash memory is a commodity-priced cyclical; EPS swung from -$11.24 to $73.76 with EBIT margin at a 100th-percentile 61.6% (10y avg 10%) - clearly peak-cycle earnings that cannot be forecast.

name: Exzeo Group, Inc.
reason: Insurance software/operations platform whose revenue is concentrated in its parent HCI Group's Florida homeowners carriers (single-customer and catastrophe-exposure risk), with EBIT margin jumping from -83% to 48.8% in three years - too short and concentrated a record.

name: Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp.
reason: BDC lending to sponsor-backed software companies: earnings set by base rates and credit losses, EPS at 0.58x its 2021 high with 5.8x leverage-type net debt and ~0 consensus growth; no route to 7%+ per-share growth.

name: Jefferson Capital, Inc.
reason: Charged-off/insolvency consumer debt buyer whose returns depend on credit cycles and purchase pricing, with 4.2x net debt/EBITDA, only two years of public history and consensus FY1 EPS -14.6%.

name: Amrize Ltd
reason: North American cement/aggregates spin-off from Holcim has local-oligopoly assets and 1.6x leverage, but EPS was flat 2022-25 ($2.00 to $2.14), 10y avg ROIC is only 6.5%, and earnings are tied to construction and roofing cycles plus a new standalone structure.

name: McGraw Hill, Inc.
reason: Sponsor-owned education publisher with 3.1x net debt/EBITDA, GAAP EPS only $0.19 vs large adjusted add-backs, consensus growth ~3-5% and a credible AI disintermediation threat to courseware/assessment content.

name: NIQ Global Intelligence PLC
reason: Consumer-panel/retail-measurement data franchise (Nielsen legacy) with a real data moat, but GAAP losses every year (EPS -$1.20 in 2025), 5.9% EBIT margin, 3.8x net debt/EBITDA under Advent ownership and AI-driven analytics competition make it hard to forecast.

name: StubHub Holdings Incorporation
reason: Secondary ticketing marketplace with GAAP losses (EPS -$5.76 in 2025, EBIT margin -71%), acquisitions at 32x FCF, regulatory threat from all-in pricing/FTC and anti-scalping rules, and dependence on event-cycle volumes.

name: Alliance Laundry Holdings, Inc.
reason: Global leader in commercial laundry equipment (Speed Queen etc.) with replacement-driven, route/laundromat demand, stable 17-19% EBIT margin, 1.33x FCF conversion and 10-12% consensus EPS growth; main caveats are 4.4x net debt/EBITDA under BDT ownership and large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap.

name: SunocoCorp LLC
reason: Motor-fuel distribution, pipelines/terminals and a refinery with 3.7% EBIT margin, 8.6x net debt/EBITDA, acquisitions at 1.75x FCF and commodity/fuel-margin exposure - fails the balance-sheet and forecastability tests.

name: Lumexa Imaging Holdings, Inc.
reason: Outpatient imaging/teleradiology operator with 11x net debt/EBITDA, GAAP losses every year and exposure to government/commercial reimbursement cuts - fails the balance-sheet and regulatory tests.

name: Versant Media Group, Inc.
reason: Comcast cable-network spin-off (CNBC/MSNBC/Golf/USA) in secular cord-cutting decline: EPS fell from $12.21 to $6.45 and EBIT margin from 30.8% to 21.1% over 2022-25.

name: Carnival Corporation Ltd.
reason: Cyclical cruise operator that lost money 2020-23, diluted shares 6.1%/yr over 10y, carries 3.6x net debt/EBITDA and EPS still only 0.51x its pre-COVID peak - fails the recession-survival and per-share growth tests.
